rendered: The solvent with the strongest hydrogen bonding is water. The paper says that[1] bonding with a δH value of 42.3 MPa^1/2[2]. This is the highest δH of any solvent plotted in Fig. 6[3], ahead of glycerol, EG and DEG. It is still not used for delamination because the aluminum foil corrodes. Lithium leaching from the NMC cathode makes the water solution basic, and the resulting aluminum corrosion would contaminate the NMC particles with aluminum hydroxide precipitates on the cathode surfaces.[4][5][6][7] The solvent the paper does use, EG, has a δh of[8] 26.0[9] in Table 1[10].
